title: Preparing a Node project
idea: `package.json` is the manifest of a Node project. It names the project, picks the module format and defines commands such as `npm start`.
points: `npm init -y` writes a starter `package.json` using default answers.
`"type": "module"` makes `.js` files ES modules, so `import` and `export` work.
A `scripts` entry names a command; `npm start` runs the `start` script.
Keep code in `src/`; `src/index.js` is the entry point `start` runs.

steps.caption: You type `npm start` in the project folder.
npm opens `package.json` and looks in `scripts` for an entry named `start`.
It finds `node src/index.js` and runs that command.
Node starts, loads `src/index.js` and reads the nearest `package.json` to learn its module type.
`"type": "module"` makes the `.js` file an ES module, so its `import` lines work.

code.title: The manifest
code.caption: A trimmed `package.json` for this project. `npm init -y` writes a starter; `npm pkg set type=module` sets a key without opening the file.

walk.text: Name and version identify the project.
`type` decides how Node reads every `.js` file in this project.
`npm start` runs this command. Other script names need `npm run`.

code.title: What ES modules change
code.caption: Run it beside that `package.json`. `.mjs` is always an ES module; `type` gives `.js` files the same rules.

pitfalls: In ES modules `require` and `__dirname` do not exist; use `import` and `import.meta.url`.
Write the extension in relative imports: `./app.js`, not `./app`.
Set `type` yourself. Without it, `.js` defaults to CommonJS and `import` may fail or warn.

quiz.why: In an ES module `require` is not defined. Use `import os from 'node:os'` instead.

takeaway: `package.json` tells npm what to run and tells Node how to read `.js`.

starters: Should I use ES modules or CommonJS in a new project?
What does `-y` skip when I run `npm init`?
Why keep code in `src/` and not in the project root?
